## Monetise

### Trust before transactions
<a id="biz-trust-before-transactions"></a>

Give value, show credibility, build relationship before selling; let content sell (soft CTA, client results, process, objections). Educational content scales trust. Test every move: will it increase or decrease trust?

> will this increase trust with my audience or decrease trust?

### Share the knowledge, sell the execution
<a id="biz-share-knowledge-sell-execution"></a>

Give the real frameworks, "not some teaser"; people realise execution is hard and pay for it. Briar gives away "the sauce": others take months to apply it.

> Don't do the watered down version, not some teaser

### Offer ladder and five money models
<a id="biz-offer-ladder"></a>

Free → lead magnet → $10–100 → $500–5K → $10K+, one offer first. Models: services, products, affiliates/sponsors (only what you use), community, ads as add-on.

> Don't start with five different offers. You're going to confuse your audience.

### Sponsor as the "pro" answer
<a id="biz-sponsor-as-smart-option"></a>

Build the sponsor into a comparison (dumb → normal → pro streamer) so the product is the pro answer, not an interruption.

### Creator pyramid: micro, mid, anchors
<a id="biz-creator-pyramid"></a>

Micro creators for volume and ad creative, mid-tier (30K–100K) as the core, a few big anchors on top. Brands pay via ad creative, seeding, affiliates, paid posts and whitelisting.

> And all three of those work in concert to make amazing marketing.

### Whitelisting vs darklisting
<a id="biz-whitelisting"></a>

Whitelisting: a brand runs the creator's own post as an ad via an ad/partnership code (often outperforms). Darklisting: an ad from the creator's account that never appears on their feed.

### Modular brief
<a id="biz-modular-brief"></a>

Two key messages, target, content type, hook inspiration (text/visual/spoken), references, mechanism, simple outline, assets, variants (CTA versions, 2–3 hooks). The best 10% of creators don't need it.

### Ad maths and the Meta test
<a id="biz-ad-maths"></a>

3:1 LTV:CAC north star; thumb stop doesn't matter if ROAS hits. Test: one concept per ad set, ~$50/day, lookalikes 3% → 10%, 3–10 distinct ads, spend 3–5× target CPA before judging.

> So CPM, CPC, thumb stop, those don't really matter in my opinion.

### Closer to the dollars, more money
<a id="biz-closer-to-dollars"></a>

Funnel: attention → CTA → landing page → lead/sale → CRM → fast touches. A landing page removes every buying objection. North stars: page conversion and close rate.

> the closer you are to the dollars, the more money you make.

### Email 1–3 a week, plain text
<a id="biz-email-cadence"></a>

Campaigns vs automated flows; 1–3 sends a week, plain text from a person (Oren). Harry: less news, more letter: time-and-place intro, 5–6 examples with conflict, no paragraph over two lines.

> send it from a person.

### Follow up with "not now" people
<a id="biz-follow-up-not-now"></a>

Content is a mini follow-up; funnel = calls × show × close + follow-up closes. Their example: 100K views → $175K/month, $536K with better follow-up (unverified). Lowercase "quick question" email.

> Not everybody is a right now person

### Ads work better with organic presence
<a id="biz-ads-need-organic"></a>

Paid ads without an organic presence give poor return; closers close 10–15% higher when the prospect can see your content (claim).

### Cold outreach: Close Friends story + Loom
<a id="biz-close-friends-loom-dm"></a>

Empty Close Friends, add only targets, post a story naming them with a 3–5 min Loom pitch (Close Friends stories sit at the top of notifications); Substack DMs are uncrowded.

### Copy is the number-one marketing skill
<a id="biz-copywriting-top-skill"></a>

Same product, different words: Snickers vs Fuse. Lifting landing-page conversion from 1% to 2% doubles growth.

> It's the number one skill in marketing.

### Team: bottleneck hires, platform owners
<a id="biz-team-hire-bottleneck"></a>

Hire for the bottleneck; platform specialists over a generalist manager; culture over skills. Platform owners split 85% primary / 15% secondary. Contractors in year 0–1, core roles in-house by years 1–3.

> If they're a generalist, if they are great at all of the platforms, they suck at all of the platforms.
